quotes.text:
Last night Congressman Schmidt voted for the Take it Down Act, which criminalizes the online sharing of explicit imagery and videos to exploit victims. The bill also requires social media platforms to remove the content within a timely manner. 
 
This content – which is becoming increasingly AI-generated – has lasting negative impacts on its victims, which are too often children. The bill now heads to President Trump’s desk to be signed into law.
The ways in which sex offenders can exploit children are multiplying as fast as online technology is evolving, [...] We need to redouble our efforts for the law to keep pace.
Ought to reflect those local preferences. [...] are going to be built in some volume, somewhere and we certainly want them built in friendly spaces.

Protecting children and families online must be a priority. Too many children have fallen victim to deepfakes and other sexually explicit AI content. The TAKE IT DOWN ACT, which is now law, is designed to empower victims to protect themselves online. https://t.co/UyqwMhOcXF

As technology evolves, the threats facing our children are changing - and our laws must keep pace.

I’m a proud cosponsor of the ENFORCE Act, which closes dangerous legal loopholes, cracks down on AI-generated child sexual abuse material, and holds predators fully accountable.

Kansas kids deserve real protection.

I was excited to advocate and vote for the Rural Health Transformation Program because it makes possible this kind of continued support to strengthen rural healthcare for years to come. This new round of investment in Kansas will help rural providers put tools like artificial intelligence, remote patient monitoring, and advanced diagnostic technology to work for their patients, while strengthening transportation so people can get to the specialized care they need,

As technology evolves, so do the threats facing kids and families, and we cannot afford to look the other way.

That’s why I’ve:

- Supported stronger investigations into online child exploitation

- Cracked down on bad actors who use AI to harm children

- Voted for the bipartisan TAKE IT DOWN Act to help remove nonconsensual intimate images and AI-generated deepfakes from the internet

- Supported legislation that gives parents more tools and control to protect their kids online

Our children deserve to grow up safe—both in their communities and online. I’ll continue fighting to give parents the tools they need and hold accountable those who seek to harm our kids.

Keeping our kids safe online is our responsibility. 

The Take It Down Act, which I helped pass into law, requires online platforms to remove intimate images shared without permission, including fake images created with AI. This helps protect young people from exploitation and gives victims a way to take back control. 

Every child deserves to feel safe online, and I’ll always stand up for their safety and protection.
